goal: Исследуй, куда гражданин Казахстана может поступить на бакалавриат по IT (Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science/AI) за границей на полный грант. Найди государственные стипендии и университеты с полным покрытием (обучение, проживание, перелёт, стипендия), например Stipendium Hungaricum, Türkiye Burslari, GKS (Корея), CSC (Китай), MEXT (Япония), DAAD, а также университеты с need-based full ride для иностранцев. Используй официальные сайты и PDF с правилами приёма, указывай год данных; если цифр нет, так и напиши.

> 
> In the 2026 funding landscape, fully funded bachelor scholarships fall into three categories. Government scholarships (Turkish Burslari, KGSP, MEXT, CSC, Stipendium Hungaricum) are the most generous because they draw from state budgets and often prioritize diplomatic relationships with Arab states. University-funded scholarships (Khalifa, Princess Nourah, Qatar University, AUB, AUS) use their own endowments and typically look for high academic merit combined with demonstrated financial need. The Government of Mongolia Scholarship requires an official secondment letter and proof of years of service. JDS, the Japan-ODA-funded programme, requires the employer's written permission and a fixed commitment to return to Mongolia. These are civil-servant routes in practice, and a private-sector or unemployed applicant will not clear them.

The genuinely open schemes are the ones with no such conditions. Erasmus Mundus has no nationality restriction at all and welcomes applicants worldwide. The ADB-Japan Scholarship Program names Mongolia among eligible citizenships and funds about 130 to 135 postgraduate awards a year. Stipendium Hungaricum and Türkiye Bursları both appear on Mongolia's own Ministry of Education bilateral-partner list with their own dated calls.

Mongolia has three application patterns and the money is distributed very unevenly across them.

Government-to-government allocations. These carry the largest numbers and run through Mongolia's Ministry of Education or the relevant embassy. China is the biggest by far: 220 Chinese Government Scholarship slots a year for Mongolian citizens in 2026/27, of which 138 were already enrolled continuing students and 82 were new places. Hungary and Turkey each run their own dated call through the Ministry — Türkiye Bursları's 2026-2027 registration ran from 10 January to 20 February 2026, extended to 25 February, with results in early August 2026.

Embassy tracks. These carry the smallest numbers and the sharpest competition. The Korean Embassy's 2026 GKS-U notice allocated Mongolia exactly two undergraduate seats.

[...]

The Government of Mongolia Scholarship requires an official secondment letter and proof of years of service. JDS, funded by Japanese ODA, requires written employer permission and a fixed commitment to return to Mongolia after study. If you are in the private sector, between jobs, or applying straight from a degree, these will not work — but Chevening, Erasmus Mundus, ADB-JSP and CSC have no such condition.

Undergraduate funding is scarcer than postgraduate here, so plan around the routes that reach that level. Türkiye Bursları runs an official dated call through Mongolia's Ministry of Education. Stipendium Hungaricum covers bachelor's study. The Chinese Government Scholarship's 220 annual slots include undergraduate places. GKS-U exists but allocated Mongolia two seats for 2026. Chevening, Fulbright, Australia Awards and ADB-JSP are all postgraduate only.

Mongolia's Ministry of Education posted the official 2026-2027 call with registration running from 10 January to 20 February 2026, extended to 25 February, and results announced in early August 2026. The cycle runs on roughly the same January-to-February pattern each year, so the practical advice is to have documents ready in December rather than waiting for the announcement.

Chevening's 2027/28 round, closing at 11:00 UTC on 6 October 2026. It needs no university offer at the point of application and sets no English test of its own, which makes it the most accessible fully funded route currently accepting applications from Mongolia.

Full-Ride Undergraduate Scholarships for International Students: The Honest Shortlist
October 12, 2026
Undergraduate Scholarships

Search “fully funded undergraduate scholarships,” and you will find lists of fifty or a hundred options. Most of those lists quietly mix in graduate programs. Fulbright, Chevening, DAAD, Clarendon, and Gates Cambridge all fund graduate study. If you are finishing high school, none of them apply to you.

The real undergraduate list is much shorter. It comes down to three groups: US colleges that cover your full financial need, a few named awards at single universities, and a handful of large government programs in Asia and Turkey. This guide sorts them by how likely you are to win one. That matters more than how famous the name sounds.

Why the list is short

Universities pay graduate students because they do research and teach. Undergraduates mostly pay their own way. So undergraduate money arrives as need-based aid or as a small number of prestige awards. That is why you can find hundreds of paid PhD positions and only a few dozen genuine undergraduate full rides.

Group one: long shots worth taking

US colleges that meet your full need

[...]

MIT admits roughly two percent of its international applicants. Strong grades alone will not carry you. You need a profile that stands out in a pool full of strong grades.

Stanford also meets full need, but it treats international applicants differently. It weighs your aid request during admission. If you ask for aid, that request becomes part of the decision. You can read the full breakdown in our guide to Harvard’s need-based aid and our step-by-step Ivy League scholarship guide.

Lester B. Pearson at the University of Toronto

Pearson names about 37 scholars a year from around the world.

[...]

Your school must nominate you, and each school nominates only one student a year. After the nomination, you apply for admission to Toronto. Then you complete a separate scholarship form that arrives as a private link.

The nomination deadline falls in early October, almost a year before you would start. For the September 2027 entry, it fell on October 9, 2026. If your school has never taken part, it must apply to join the program first. Students from Arab countries are eligible, so a Gulf student at a verified international school has a real route in. Ask your counsellor in the spring of your second-to-last school year.

NYU Abu Dhabi

NYUAD sits in the Gulf, and it funds students on need. Its packages can cover tuition, housing, meals, and health insurance.

[...]

In most countries, you apply through the Japanese embassy. Check the current call, because the application route changes between years.

South Korea, Global Korea Scholarship for undergraduates

Korea awards roughly 256 to 280 undergraduate places a year through GKS. You must be under 25 and a citizen of a partner country. The award covers tuition, airfare, a settlement allowance, and a monthly allowance of around one million won. You also get one year of Korean language training before your degree starts.

Timing matters here. The embassy track for the 2027 intake closed at the end of September 2026. A second route runs through individual Korean universities and sets its own dates, typically later in the autumn. If you missed the embassy window, ask the universities about their track.

Türkiye Bursları

Turkey funds about 5,000 new students a year. Undergraduate applicants must be under 21 and need roughly a 70 percent academic record.

Harvard, Yale, Princeton, MIT, Amherst and Dartmouth appear on every published list for international applicants. Some guides add Bowdoin, the University of Notre Dame, Brown and Washington and Lee, though the lists disagree and some policies apply only to recent entering classes. Confirm any university’s current policy on its own financial aid page.

These universities fund through need-based grants. They do not run merit scholarships. A family with high demonstrated need can receive a package close to a full ride. A family with lower need receives less.

Admission remains the hurdle. Acceptance rates at these universities sit in single digits for international applicants.

Named Merit Scholarships

Several universities run merit awards that reach international students.

| Scholarship | University | Coverage | Selection route | 

| John M.

[...]

Many 2027–28 deadlines in several countries fell between April and June 2026, while others run later in 2026. Check your country’s page now.

Chevening Scholarships (United Kingdom)

Chevening is the UK government’s fully funded scholarship for one-year master’s degrees. It covers tuition, a monthly living allowance, return flights, UK visa fees and an arrival allowance.

Applicants need a bachelor’s degree, two years of work experience, leadership potential and citizenship of an eligible country. The 2027 intake window opened on 4 August 2026 and closed on 6 October 2026. Shortlisted applicants interview in March and April 2027, and results arrive from mid-June 2027.

Chevening scholars must return to their home country for a minimum period after the award. Plan for that condition before applying.

Gates Cambridge Scholarship (United Kingdom)

[...]

interviews March–April 2027 | 
| Fulbright Foreign Student (2027–28) | Set by country; many windows closed, some still open | 

Common Mistakes Applicants Make

| Mistake | Why it fails | Fix | 

| Mixing up “full ride” and “fully funded” | You apply to awards at the wrong level | Search by level first | 
| Expecting aid from need-aware universities | Financial need can lower admission odds at these universities | Prioritize need-blind or named-scholarship universities | 
| Treating need-blind as merit aid | Need-blind universities mostly give need-based grants only | Read the aid policy before you apply | 
| Assuming one global deadline | Fulbright deadlines vary by country | Use your national commission page | 
| Writing one essay for every award | Reviewers detect generic statements quickly | Tailor each essay to the award’s mission | 
| Filing aid forms late | Late forms can reduce or remove aid | Submit financial forms with the application | 
| Ignoring award conditions | Return-home or residency rules can bind you after graduation | Read terms before applying | 
| Applying only to full-funding awards | Competition is intense | Add partial-funding backups | 
| Trusting unsourced lists | Many lists repeat outdated or unverified claims | Verify on official pages | 

Previous Years’ Trends

Public data on the number of full ride awards given to international students does not exist in one place.

[...]

They do not show that full ride awards became easier or harder to win.

Research Notes

These notes record points that most guides miss.
Need-blind lists disagree. Published lists count six, nine or ten need-blind universities for international applicants, and some policies apply only to recent entering classes. The six consistent names are Harvard, Yale, Princeton, MIT, Amherst and Dartmouth.
Need-blind does not mean merit. Need-blind universities fund through need-based grants only. Applicants hunting for merit scholarships must look at other universities.
“Full ride” is a level signal. Undergraduate pages use “full ride.” Postgraduate pages use “fully funded.” Searching both terms surfaces different awards.
Deadlines depend on cycle position. As of 31 October 2026, the Chevening 2027 intake is closed, Gates Cambridge is open until 8 December 2026 or 6 January 2027, and US undergraduate regular decision opens the next wave.
Unsourced statistics circulate widely.

[...]

Fully funded usually describes postgraduate awards covering tuition plus a living stipend, airfare and insurance. Both aim to remove study costs, but the components differ by award, so read each coverage list before applying.

Do need-blind universities offer merit scholarships?

Mostly no. Need-blind universities such as Harvard, Yale, Princeton and MIT award need-based aid only. Admission ignores your finances, and the university then meets your demonstrated need through grants. A merit scholarship requires a different type of university, such as Davidson College, which runs named merit awards.

What GPA do I need for a full ride scholarship?

No single GPA applies. Most merit full rides select applicants at the top of their school class, with strong test scores where required.

Many programs add further benefits: a preparatory year for language (Turkish Burslari, KGSP, MEXT all include a dedicated language year), a free laptop (AUB, some UDST cohorts), book and stationery allowances (Qatar University, UDST Amiri), settlement grants on arrival (Turkish Burslari provides a one-time arrival payment), and exit grants upon graduation. This differs sharply from "partial" scholarships that cover only tuition (forcing the family to fund $15,000+ per year in living costs) or "merit discount" programs that reduce fees by 30–50% without touching housing or stipend.

In the 2026 funding landscape, fully funded bachelor scholarships fall into three categories. Government scholarships (Turkish Burslari, KGSP, MEXT, CSC, Stipendium Hungaricum) are the most generous because they draw from state budgets and often prioritize diplomatic relationships with Arab states. University-funded scholarships (Khalifa, Princess Nourah, Qatar University, AUB, AUS) use their own endowments and typically look for high academic merit combined with demonstrated financial need. Multilateral and religious scholarships (Islamic Development Bank, Islamic University of Madinah) serve specific populations — IsDB targets students from member Muslim countries, while IUM specifically recruits male Arabic-speaking students for Islamic studies.

The mathematics of self-funded undergraduate study in 2026 are brutal. A four-year bachelor's degree at a mid-tier U.S.

[...]

By the way, Truescho has a dedicated bachelor scholarships section + Apply-For-Me service that handles documentation, translations, and personal statement reviews end-to-end for Arab high school graduates.


One of the biggest obstacles for Arab high school graduates is the SAT — a $112 test that requires weeks of preparation and is not part of the Arab school curriculum. Fortunately, several top-tier bachelor scholarships in 2026 waive SAT and ACT requirements entirely for applicants whose national high school system is standardized by a recognized government authority. The confirmed SAT-optional or SAT-waiver programs for the 2026 cycle include: Türkiye Burslari (never required SAT), KGSP Undergraduate (never required SAT), MEXT Japan (uses its own EJU exam on arrival), CSC China (rarely requires SAT for non-English programs), Stipendium Hungaricum (no SAT needed), Azerbaijan Government, IsDB Scholarship, and Shanghai Government SGS.

NYU Abu Dhabi announced for 2026 that SAT scores are "optional" — applicants without scores are reviewed holistically, and Arab applicants with 95%+ secondary certificates are not disadvantaged. Khalifa University accepts the SAT but also reviews IBT, A-Levels, and IB scores; Saudi and Emirati national curriculum scores are also accepted.

[...]

Academic evaluation is based on high school transcripts, personal statement, and study plan.

Princess Nourah University requires a minimum 85% secondary certificate for undergraduate scholarship applicants, but competitive admitted students typically present 92%+ scores. The program is exclusively for female applicants, prioritizes Saudi nationals, and extends scholarships to international Arab female students in specific majors including medicine, pharmacy, nursing, and computer science.

Yes. Türkiye Burslari, KGSP Korea, MEXT Japan, CSC China (non-English programs), Azerbaijan Government, IsDB, Shanghai Government SGS, and Reach Oxford all accept applications without IELTS. Alternatives include the Medium of Instruction (MOI) letter, Duolingo English Test, or in-country testing upon arrival. Full list in our scholarships without IELTS 2026 guide.

MEXT Undergraduate applications for 2027 intake open at Japanese embassies worldwide in April–May 2026, with deadlines typically in early June. The process includes written exams in mathematics and English (or Japanese), followed by an embassy interview. Successful applicants start Japanese language preparation in April 2027 before beginning undergraduate study in September 2027.

Government scholarships (Türkiye Burslari, KGSP, MEXT, CSC) are funded by state budgets, cover every cost, and usually include a mandatory language preparation year. University scholarships (Khalifa, Princess Nourah, HBKU, AUB) are funded by institutional endowments, target specific faculties, and often require higher standardized test scores. Government programs accept more applicants; university programs often pay slightly higher stipends.

Most fully funded bachelor scholarships cover round-trip airfare at least once — some annually. Türkiye Burslari covers arrival and final departure flights. KGSP covers arrival only.

[...]

Khalifa University and UDST Amiri include annual return flights for international students. Princess Nourah covers arrival and one annual ticket. Always verify airfare coverage in the specific scholarship agreement.

Fully funded bachelor scholarships in 2026 represent the single best path for academically capable Arab high school graduates to access world-class education without the $150,000+ tuition trap. The 20 programs profiled in this monthly-updated guide — from Türkiye Burslari's generous stipend-plus-language structure to Princess Nourah's unique opportunity for Saudi and international female students, from KGSP's one-year Korean prep to NYU Abu Dhabi's need-blind admissions — cover every major world region, every field of study, and every combination of GPA and test-score profile. The applicants who succeed in 2026 will not be those with the highest single score, but those who start preparing 12–18 months early, apply to 5–8 programs in parallel, draft personal statements that are genuinely tailored to each country, and verify every document against official portal requirements. Bookmark this page, set calendar reminders for February and October 2026 (the two biggest deadline clusters), and start building your application portfolio now.

For graduate-level follow-up, see our fully funded master's scholarships 2026 guide.

Türkiye Bursları (Türkiye Scholarships) 2027: Coverage, Eligibility and How to Apply

Updated 25 October 2026, adding our method for choosing the 12 programmes. This guide also includes our former guide for Pakistani students. Scholarship rules come from the official Türkiye Scholarships site (turkiyeburslari.gov.tr); Pakistani award numbers come from the Turkish Embassy event reported in September 2025; the China and Hungary comparison comes from HEC's 2026–27 calls. The official calendar repeats yearly without printing the year, so confirm the 2027 dates when the call opens.

Türkiye Bursları is the Turkish government's fully funded scholarship for international students at bachelor's, master's and PhD level. It covers tuition, accommodation, health insurance, a one-year Turkish course, a return flight and a monthly stipend of 6,500 TL (bachelor's), 9,500 TL (master's) or 13,000 TL (PhD). Citizens of every country except Türkiye can apply, online, for free and without any nomination, choosing up to 12 programmes.

[...]

No minimum language score is stated for the standard scholarship. In 2025, 166 Pakistani students were selected.

Türkiye Bursları at a glance

| Question | Official answer | 

| Levels | Associate degree, bachelor's, master's, PhD, art programmes, a Merit Scholarship and a research scholarship | 
| Monthly stipend | Bachelor's 6,500 TL; master's 9,500 TL; PhD 13,000 TL (Merit Scholarship holders get twice the regular stipend) | 
| Also covered | University placement, tuition, accommodation, health insurance, one-year Turkish course, one flight at the start and one at graduation | 
| Nationality | All countries; not Turkish citizens or people who lost Turkish citizenship | 
| Age limits | Under 21 (bachelor's), under 30 (master's), under 35 (PhD), under 50 (research) | 
| Minimum grades | 70% (bachelor's), 75% (master's and PhD), 90% for medicine, dentistry and pharmacy | 
| Application fee | None. You apply online for free | 
| Programme choices | Up to 12 | 
| General call | Usually 10 January – 20 February | 

What does Türkiye Bursları cover?

Türkiye Bursları places you at a Turkish university and pays:
Full tuition at the university you are placed in.

[...]

The official site sets three rules for your choices: you can only pick from the universities and departments the portal offers for your educational background, the committee judges how consistent your choices are, and you should check the equivalence and validity of each field in your own country before you apply. Within those rules, this is the method we suggest:

1. Pick one field family, not one subject. For an FSc pre-engineering student interested in computing, that might be computer engineering, software engineering and electrical-electronics engineering. Those choices tell one story; adding business administration and nursing does not.
2. Check the teaching language of every programme. Many are taught in Turkish after the funded language year, some in English. A mix is fine, but know which is which before your interview, because you may be asked.
3. Spread your choices across universities. This is our suggestion, not an official rule: placing all 12 at the best-known universities in Istanbul and Ankara means competing with the most applicants for the same places.

[...]

HUF 140,000 to 180,000 (PhD) | 
| Housing | Accommodation covered | On-campus room or a housing allowance | Free dormitory place or HUF 40,000 a month | 
| Age limits | Under 21 / 30 / 35 | Under 25 / 35 / 40 | Set by the call and HEC | 
| Language | Funded one-year Turkish course; many programmes in Turkish | Chinese-taught programmes need HSK; some English-taught programmes | Many English-taught programmes; two semesters of Hungarian for full-time bachelor's and master's students | 
| Last deadline | Usually 20 February | HEC portal: 5 January 2026 | 15 January 2026, 16:00 Pakistan time | 

Which one fits which student? Türkiye suits applicants who want the most complete package, with housing, flights and a language year all covered, and who are comfortable studying partly in Turkish. Hungary suits students who want an English-taught degree inside the EU and can add some money of their own, because the bachelor's and master's stipend is only about €110 a month. China suits postgraduate applicants who are ready to contact a supervisor early, because a pre-acceptance letter is often the deciding document.

[...]

Is there an application fee?

No. Applying for Türkiye Bursları is free.

COMPSAC is the IEEE Computer Society Signature Conference on Computers, Software and Applications. It is a major international forum for academia, industry, and government to discuss research results and advancements, emerging challenges, and future trends in computer and software technologies and applications. The theme of COMPSAC 2022 is “Computers, Software, and Applications in an Uncertain World”.

It is clear that we are heading towards an uncertain world catalyzed by the consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic and ongoing political disputes. This uncertainty has significant and direct implications for all aspects of the computer industry. To thrive in this increasingly uncertain world, innovations of computer hardware, software, and applications have emerged as a pressing need. The emerging interconnected world demands new developments in sensor-based communication hardware and operating systems. Software engineering continues to prove essential to our daily lives ranging from financial services, health care, remote learning platforms, social networks to the era of connected and autonomous vehicles, and artificial intelligence control. Governing organizations have responded to this trend by defining regulations and standards to address issues such as safety, security, and resiliency of computer hardware and software systems and applications. However, unique challenges originate from mandating these requirements under uncertainty in the absence of sound and complete solutions applicable to these new types of systems and applications. As computer researchers, we see these challenges as opportunities to fill gaps in how all dimensions of computing are developed, utilized, and supported. How to improve the resiliency of these components across a wide range of use domains is a significant challenge we suddenly find ourselves facing. How do we design systems that are able to withstand the stress of global-scale use, and still provide robust and secure services to end-users? For over 45 years, COMPSAC has been an outlet for researchers to share and discuss innovative and novel approaches to problems such as these, and we look forward to hearing your ideas in 2022!

COMPSAC 2022, organized as a tightly integrated union of symposia, will focus on technical aspects of issues relevant to computers, software and applications, with an emphasis on topics related to improving collaboration with intelligence and resilience. The technical program will include keynote addresses, research papers, industrial case studies, fast abstracts, a doctoral symposium, poster sessions, and workshops and tutorials on emerging and important topics related to the conference theme. Highlights of the conference will include plenary and specialized panels that will address the technical challenges facing researchers and practitioners who are driving fundamental changes in *Computers, Software, and Applications in an Uncertain World.* Panels will also address cultural and societal challenges with respect to computing and collaboration raised by rapidly changing communication norms.

Authors are invited to submit original, unpublished research work, as well as industrial practice reports. Simultaneous submission to other publication venues is not permitted except as highlighted in the COMPSAC 2022 JC & CJ program. All submissions must adhere to IEEE Publishing Policies and will be vetted through the IEEE CrossCheck portal.
